evidence:
packaging/install.sh:134-140
  answer=$("$1/bin/fn" operator "$config" status 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  ...
  case $answer in *reason=store-format*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || echo "install: status answered $rc (see above); the store is not a format refusal, so this continues"
  return 0
fix: Have ask() continue only on rc 0 or on the stopped-node exit that status documents for a healthy stopped store (18 not-running). Treat every other code as a refusal, so the store is not switched and the node restarts on the release it ran. Name the class (refused, fenced, fault) in the message.
reviewer: packaging/install.sh:131-141: ask() returns 1 only when the output contains reason=store-format. Any other non-zero rc (packaging/fn:104-106 heap-probe fault, exit 4; fenced exit 3; usage 5) prints a 'this continues' note and returns 0. Callers at :268-277 (upgrade), :294-302 (rollback) and :327 (install) then switch_to, render_service, start_node and health_wait. health_wait exits 4 after 180 s and never restores previous. That breaks the header's promise at :42-44 that a refusal puts nothing in place. Treating rc != 0 as continue is deliberate (the message says so), but a fault or fence from the next release is still allowed to switch current.
scenario: An operator runs --upgrade to a release whose image cannot run on this machine. For example, the heap probe faults (packaging/fn:104 'fault heap-probe-did-not-run', exit 4), libssl 3 is missing, or the store answers exit 3 (fenced: recover before further mutation). ask() prints the rc and returns 0. switch_to then points current at the new release, render_service installs its unit and start_node runs. health_wait then times out after 180 s and exits 4. The node is left down on a release that already said it could not open the store, and nothing switches it back. This breaks the header's promise (lines 42-44) that 'a refusal puts nothing in place'. The same applies to --rollback (line 294) and to a first install over an existing fn.toml (line 327). Uncertain (3), fault (4) and usage (5) all end up in the accepted path.
title: install.sh --upgrade/--rollback/install: ask() only refuses on the literal reason=store-format. Every other failure, including fault, fenced and a probe that never ran, carries on and switches current
